The formalization of sEr as the product of sHR and D establishes a multiplicative kernel for predicting behavioral output. This formulation implies that action potentiality is not additive but rather emergent from the interaction of learned behavior and motivational force. The derivation hinges on the assumption that sEr is a deterministic function of sHR and D, which allows for probabilistic modeling in GSI and state transition logic in GSE. Failure modes include saturation of sHR or D, leading to loss of sensitivity in sEr predictions. The system assumes a linear relationship between components, which may not hold under extreme conditions or when non-linear feedback loops are introduced.
